# The major business players

This chapter maps the field. For each company the questions that matter for investing are: **how big is it, how AC-focused is it (a little or a lot of the business), what is its share of the industry, and is it levered to the high-growth parts (commercial, applied, data center, premium efficiency)?** Figures below are approximate first-pass numbers — the financial chapter and later deepening will tighten them against primary filings.

## The global leaders by AC volume

The global air-conditioning equipment industry is led by a handful of names that recur across rankings: **Daikin, Midea, Gree, Haier, and Carrier**, with **Mitsubishi Electric, LG, Samsung, Johnson Controls, and Trane** close behind.[^rank] Asia-Pacific is the center of gravity, accounting for roughly **47%** of industry revenue.

[^rank]: Spherical Insights, "Top 20 HVAC Companies in Global 2025" (<https://www.sphericalinsights.com/blogs/top-20-hvac-companies-in-global-2025-statistics-view-by-spherical-insights-and-consulting>); Mordor Intelligence air-conditioner market report. Rankings differ by whether they count units, revenue, or HVAC broadly.

## The cleanest "AC growth" exposures

**Daikin Industries** — The world's largest air-conditioning maker, operating in 170+ countries, with AC as essentially its whole business. It reported record results for the fiscal year ended March 2025 (~¥4 trillion / ~€29 billion in net sales), led by applied and commercial AC and by strength in India and Japan [@daikin2024results]. It is the purest large-cap bet on the global cooling story, but trades in Tokyo and at a premium.

**Carrier Global** — Spun out of United Technologies in 2020, Carrier has reshaped itself into a **pure-play HVAC** company: it acquired Viessmann Climate Solutions (European heat pumps) and divested its Fire & Security and commercial-refrigeration businesses [@carrier2024]. That makes it one of the most direct U.S.-listed ways to own residential-plus-commercial cooling and the heat-pump transition. Reported revenue is roughly \$20+ billion.

**Trane Technologies** — A **pure-play climate** company, more commercial- and applied-weighted than Carrier, plus the Thermo King transport-refrigeration franchise. ~\$22.5 billion revenue [@trane2024]. Frequently the market's preferred "quality" name in the group; the question is always valuation.

**Lennox International** — The most concentrated **North American** play (~\$5.2 billion revenue), spanning residential, commercial, and refrigeration, with a 2024 ductless/VRF **joint venture with Samsung** extending its product range [@lennox2024]. Smaller and U.S.-centric, so more exposed to the domestic replacement and refrigerant cycle.

## The "AC is a small part of a giant" names

**Mitsubishi Electric** — The Air Conditioning Systems & Home Products segment generated roughly **\$9.4 billion** in FY2024 and the company is a global VRF/ductless leader [@mitsubishi2024ir] — but that segment is only one part of a sprawling industrial conglomerate (factory automation, power, semiconductors). You get genuine AC leadership diluted by unrelated businesses.

**LG and Samsung** — Both are serious in ductless/VRF and (for LG) **data-center cooling**, where LG cited ~\$720 million of regional orders in 2024 — but AC is a modest slice of each company's enormous electronics revenue. Exposure is real but diluted.

**Johnson Controls** — Pivoting *away* from equipment toward commercial building solutions, controls, and service; it **completed the sale of its residential and light-commercial HVAC business to Bosch (~\$8 billion) in August 2025** [@jci2024sale]. It is now more a "smart buildings / service" story than an AC-equipment story — and the deal made **Bosch** a major U.S. residential player overnight (see the [market-share chapter](market-share.qmd)).

**Vertiv** is the cleanest *data-center-cooling* adjacency and is profiled in full — business, segments, growth, backlog, and risks — in the [data-center cooling chapter](data-center-cooling.qmd), alongside Modine and nVent. For **European** growth specifically, the best-positioned listed names are **Carrier** (via its Viessmann heat-pump acquisition), **Daikin**, **NIBE** (Stockholm), and **Mitsubishi Electric**, with Bosch and Vaillant relevant but private — see the [market chapter](03-market-size-growth.qmd#who-is-positioned-for-european-growth-your-specific-interest).

::: {.callout-note}
**Investor takeaway.** If the goal is *concentrated* exposure to the cooling-and-efficiency growth story via liquid public equity, the shortlist is short: **Daikin** (global, purest, Tokyo-listed), **Carrier** and **Trane** (U.S.-listed pure-plays), and **Lennox** (North-America-concentrated). **Vertiv** is the cleanest *data-center-cooling* adjacency. The conglomerates (Mitsubishi, LG, Samsung, JCI) and the Chinese volume leaders (Midea, Gree, Haier) round out the picture but each comes with a "what am I really buying" caveat.
:::
